Let me analyze this conflict.

Register says: "Elster Metering Ltd"
Document says: "Elster Water Metering Limited"

The rules say:
- spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity
- Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's)

"Elster Metering Ltd" vs "Elster Water Metering Limited" — is "Water" a spelling drift? No, it's an additional word that changes the company name. Elster Metering Ltd and Elster Water Metering Limited could genuinely be different legal entities — actually, in reality, Elster Water Metering Limited is the correct legal name (formerly Elster Metering Ltd, renamed around 2012-2014). But per the rules as given: is "Water" insertion a spelling drift or legal-suffix drift? The suffix drift is "Ltd" vs "Limited" — that's legal-suffix drift. But "Metering" vs "Water Metering" is an added word, not just suffix drift.

Hmm. The certificate is from 2014 (issuing_year: 2014). The company Elster Metering Ltd was renamed Elster Water Metering Limited. So they're the same entity historically. But strictly by name comparison, "Elster Metering Ltd" vs "Elster Water Metering Limited" — the distinguishing token "Water" differs.

The rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Is "Elster Metering Ltd" vs "Elster Water Metering Limited" genuinely different? The word "Water" is a meaningful differentiator, not just spelling/suffix/accent drift. By strict application of the rules, this would be different-entity, and best_value = document's value: "Elster Water Metering Limited".

The certificate is the legal instrument, and the legal entity name on the certificate at issuing time (2014) would be Elster Water Metering Limited. The register likely has an older name.

Verdict: different-entity, best_value: "Elster Water Metering Limited".

Alternatively one could argue same-entity because it's the same company renamed — but the rules only allow same-entity for spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences. An inserted word "Water" changes the name meaningfully. The rule for genuinely different names = different-entity with document value. Since the certificate is the legal instrument, the fused record should carry the certificate's name.

I'll go with different-entity, best_value = "Elster Water Metering Limited".

Why: one short sentence. "The document name inserts 'Water', which is more than suffix/spelling drift, so treat as a distinct legal name; the certificate as legal instrument supplies the authoritative value."
